note: A pass naming an arc that is not in the network (SPEC 6.2). A walk is used whole or not at all, so the highlight carrying it is dropped: keeping the first pass alone would hand the caller a walk that ends at b, which nobody drew. Exactly one diagnostic is expected, at the pass: the first problem in a walk is reported and nothing after it is examined. The second highlight is valid and survives, so a reader that dropped every highlight in the network on one bad walk fails `counts`. The survivor carries a position so that `positions` pins WHICH highlight survived: counts alone cannot tell the good highlight from the bad one.
